summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for volume overload due to decompensated cirrhosis and portopulmonary hypertension. He presented with worsening ascites and bilateral lower extremity edema refractory to oral diuretics. During the 8-day admission, he received aggressive IV diuresis and underwent a therapeutic paracentesis, removing 7.6 liters of fluid. His weight decreased from 101 kg to 93.9 kg. A right heart catheterization was performed, showing a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 24 mmHg, indicating improved pulmonary hemodynamics. He remained on chronic medications including treprostinil, spironolactone, and rifaximin. He was discharged home with an increased dose of torsemide, instructions to monitor daily weight, and plans for weekly paracenteses and outpatient follow-up.
